title: Isolated VPC upgrade blueprint: staged artifact diffusion, operatorless rollback and minimal-egress acceptance criteria
creator: Amrita Kaur
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers operate Redwood Private in fully isolated VPCs or air-gapped racks and have asked for a deterministic, low-egress upgrade flow that supports: staged artifact diffusion to mirrors, operatorless (minimal human) rollback triggers, and runtime degradation modes when external telemetry is unavailable. This doc defines a product blueprint and acceptance criteria for a "minimal-egress upgrade" mode that preserves safety, auditability, and the ability to rollback without opening broad egress windows.

Goals:
- Define upgrade orchestration contracts that work with zero-or-minimal-egress policies (egress consent windows, signed bundles, mirror-first diffusion).
- Provide operatorless rollback primitives (automated health fences + signed rollback manifests) so customers can meet strict change-control policies.
- Ensure all artifacts have provenance (manifest signatures, checksums, signed image indexes) and that offline verification is possible with customer KMS or provided public keys.
- Offer telemetry fallbacks and graceful runtime degradation modes when outbound telemetry is blocked.

Scope (in):
- Upgrade orchestration flow for control-plane/operator interactions in private VPC and air-gapped installs.
- Staged artifact diffusion tooling (mirror promotion, verification, compact delta bundles).
- Acceptance criteria and test harness for network-limited upgrade scenarios.
- Rollout and automatic rollback guard definitions tied to health signals.

Scope (out):
- Building new container registries or physical media distribution (customers may use their existing mirror infra).
- Low-level kernel or hardware patching workflows outside Redwood operator lifecycle.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Customers may permit a narrow egress window (egress consent) or none at all; design must support both.
- Targeted clusters may be behind private proxies, with limited bandwidth to mirrors.
- Customers require cryptographic artifact verification; we must not assume trust in intermediate mirrors.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Full offline upgrades (physical media) vs. staged mirror-first upgrades: we prioritize mirror-first with optional physical media fallbacks to reduce operational burden.
- Telemetry completeness vs. privacy/compliance: provide configurable telemetry levels (none/minimal/diagnostic) with local buffering and encrypted outbox for postponed upload during consent windows.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Artifact provenance - Every upgrade bundle (operator image, runtime artifacts, manifests) must include a signed manifest.json and SHA256 checksums. Signatures must be verifiable using either a Redwood public key bundle or the customer's provided public key. Verification must succeed offline (no external HTTPs required) using locally-staged keys.

AC-2: Mirror-first diffusion - Upgrade orchestration supports a two-phase diffusion: (1) push to customer mirrors (pull-based); (2) promote mirror to release. The controller must be able to validate mirror integrity before promotion without contacting Redwood central services.

AC-3: Minimal-egress protocol - When an egress-consent window is allowed, the system must only contact specified hostnames/IP ranges and must limit transfer to declared artifact digests. All egress endpoints for a given upgrade must be declared in the upgrade manifest and enforced by the operator.

AC-4: Operatorless rollback trigger - The operator exposes automated rollback fences: if a configured set of health signals degrade (pod restart rate, 95th latency, model bootstrap failure) for more than a defined SLA window, the operator rolls back to the previous signed manifest without human approval. This behavior must be configurable per-cluster.

AC-5: Offline verification flow - Customers can validate bundle integrity and signature using the CLI tool (--offline-verify) against a local keyring; the tool must reproduce the operator's verification decisions and report mismatches with deterministic exit codes for automation.

AC-6: Compact delta bundles - Upgrades may be delivered as delta bundles; the operator must validate base-image checksums before applying a delta and must be able to reconstruct the full artifact from local base + delta and validate final checksum before activation.

AC-7: KMS rotation compatibility - The upgrade flow must allow cust-managed KMS rotations: manifests reference key IDs rather than raw public keys, and the operator supports a key-rollover verification step with configurable grace windows.

AC-8: Telemetry graceful degradation - When telemetry egress is blocked, runtime changes to reduced-observability mode: aggregated samples only, no PII, and local ring-buffered events preserved and tagged for deferred upload during consent windows. System health dashboards must still show degraded-but-functional status locally.

AC-9: Canaries without external traffic - Support canary selection that relies on internal traffic and synthetic probes when public-facing traffic cannot be used for canaries. Synthetic probes must be definable in the upgrade manifest and executed locally.

AC-10: Audit and operator logs - All upgrade steps (pull, verify, stage, activate, rollback) must be logged with timestamps, manifest digest, verifier identity, and local-node checksums; logs must be exportable to customer log sinks and redacted according to configured policies.

AC-11: Zero-trust image provenance - If a mirror presents inconsistent digests across nodes, the operator must fail the promotion and mark the mirror as quarantined; promotion only succeeds when >95% of mirror replicas report matching checksums.

AC-12: Time-bounded egress consent - The UI/CLI flow must allow customers to open a time-limited egress consent window that automatically closes; all artifacts pulled during the window are validated and recorded. The operator will refuse additional egress outside declared digests during the window.

AC-13: Test harness - Provide an automated test harness that simulates limited-bandwidth mirrors, intermittent network partition, and zero-egress scenarios; the harness must be runnable in CI by customers to validate upgrade recipes.

AC-14: Backward compatibility - New upgrade artifacts must include a compatibility matrix showing minimum runtime and operator versions required for rollback to remain possible; operator refuses upgrades that would make immediate rollback impossible.

AC-15: Documentation and runbook - A runbook for RG/NetOps must exist describing step-by-step guided upgrade, emergency manual rollback using signed manifests, and forensic verification steps for regulators.

AC-16: Compliance-friendly telemetry - When configured to 'compliance' mode, telemetry is limited to vector-of-booleans health flags; this mode must still trigger automated rollback fences without exposing payloads or user inputs.
test_plan: TP-1: Offline-verify smoke test - Use the CLI to verify a signed test bundle with the provided local keyring; expect exit code 0 and a matching digest report.
TP-2: Mirror integrity validation - Start 3 mirror replicas with divergent files; run promotion and expect operator to quarantine the mirrors and fail promotion (non-zero exit + audit entry).

TP-3: Minimal-egress treadmill - Simulate a declared egress window; instrumentation ensures only declared hostnames were contacted and transfer sizes match manifest. Verify audit log contains transfer hashes.

TP-4: Operatorless rollback simulation - Deploy a canary that intentionally fails synthetic probes; confirm operator detects degradation and performs signed rollback automatically. Verify rollback manifest recorded in audit logs.

TP-5: Telemetry blocked run - Block outbound telemetry endpoints; upgrade and intentionally trigger a minor misconfiguration; ensure runtime enters degraded telemetry mode and rollback still occurs based on local diagnostics.
TP-6: KMS rotation test - Rotate a test KMS key and verify operator accepts bundle signed by new key after grace window; pre-rotation bundles remain verifiable.
TP-7: Delta bundle reconstruction - Apply delta bundles against a base image and validate reconstructed artifact checksum equals expected full bundle checksum.
TP-8: Performance under bandwidth cap - Run a large bundle transfer with limited bandwidth (50Mbps) and verify promotion completes within acceptable time or aborts with explicit reason in audit log.
TP-9: CI harness - Integrate the test harness into a sample CI job that emulates private VPC topology and runs TP-1..TP-8 in sequence.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha with 2 SRE partners and dedicated staging mirrors. Phase 1: Invite-only early customers (up to 5) with signed NDA to pilot mirror-first upgrades and operatorless rollback. Phase 2: Gradual beta with UI/CLI features enabled and egress consent flow in Console. Phase 3: GA with documentation, runbooks, and migration guides. Each phase gated by passing all test-plan items and receiving sign-off from security/compliance reviewers.
